Subject: Our app seeing intermittent 504s + big tail latency spike (Greenfield account)

Hi Rachel —

We started seeing a spike in 504 timeouts and very high p95/p99 latency on Redwood API calls affecting our checkout flows at ~08:50 PST. Approximately 6% of token requests returned 504 over the last 30 minutes and the UI is timing out for customers.

We've attached a short metrics screenshot and a capture from our edge (we can share full pcaps to support). Can you confirm whether there were any changes on Redwood side (deploys, routing, peering changes) around 08:30–09:00? This is impacting the Black Friday promo traffic and we need an ETA for mitigation.

Alex Morgan

- Check for NAT port exhaustion or proxy 504s on our egress proxies.
- If peering path instability is suspected, recommend temporary routing to alternate peer + enable short-circuit fallback to cold cache (if safe) to mitigate timeouts.

Jonas: please start with live packet captures and the connection-rate counters. Vivek: I’m flagging this for executive visibility — if this requires capacity changes or SLA credits we need to know quickly.

Subject: RE: Fwd: Our app seeing intermittent 504s + big tail latency spike — initial findings

Quick update from SRE triage (initial 30-min window):
- Correlated Greenfield request IDs trace to egress node eu-west-2->us-west-2 path that shows intermittent reroute via EdgeNet transit.
- Packet captures (attached) show repeated SYN retransmits and a number of TCP connections hitting idle timeouts on the proxy layer; several 504s are generated by the outbound proxy, not by our model-serving tier.
- Connection pool counters on the egress proxies show brief spikes in ephemeral port usage consistent with NAT exhaustion symptoms (spikes align with customer's burst).

Immediate mitigation plan (recommended):
1) Short-term: steer Greenfield traffic to alternate peering (us-west alternate peer) and increase ephemeral port range on egress proxies by +20% to reduce NAT collisions. This should reduce observed 504s within 5–10 minutes.
2) Mid-term: coordinate with EdgeNet to investigate the transit reroute and hold a postmortem; request EdgeNet to confirm no maintenance or policy changes.
3) Customer comms: Marissa/Neha to send a brief status update and estimated time to mitigation.

Attachments: packet-captures.zip (sample pcaps), internal_trace_greenfield_0800-0900.log

Subject: Re: Fwd: Our app seeing intermittent 504s + big tail latency spike — mitigation and exec summary

Good work triaging — Jonas, thanks for the packet captures and clear mitigation steps. Confirming the actions we executed:
- Routing rule change applied at 09:58 PST to steer Greenfield via alternate us-west peer; saw immediate drop in 504s from ~6% to ~0.5% over the next 10 minutes.
- Ephemeral port pool expanded and proxy socket backlog tuning applied; no service restarts required.
- EdgeNet acknowledged a transient routing flap; they’ve opened INC-8921 and will correlate with their peering controller logs.

Next steps / exec asks:
- Prepare a short MOP and customer-facing timeline (Marissa/Neha) — include what we changed, why, and planned long-term remediation (peering resilience, port pool autoscaling).
- Postmortem with EdgeNet + internal RCA within 72 hours. Assign owners and timelines.
- Finance: if customer requests, we’ll review appropriate credits per SLA — hold for PM and Legal review.

I’ve attached the network playbook excerpt for temporary routing and runbook steps. Rachel — please schedule an exec 15-min brief if the customer requests a deeper commitment.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
Attachments: runbook_network_playbook.pdf

Alex — thanks again for the quick sample traces and patience. Short recap for the thread and the customer-facing note we’ll send:
- What happened: transient peering reroute via EdgeNet caused higher RTTs and proxy socket churn; combined with a customer burst this triggered proxy-side 504s (observed NAT port pressure).
- What we did: short-term traffic steering to alternate us-west peer and ephemeral port tuning, which reduced 504s to acceptable levels.
- Next steps: full RCA with EdgeNet within 72 hours, permanent peering resilience changes, and automated port-pool autoscaling to prevent similar bursts.

Marissa/Neha — please send the status note to Alex+procurement and copy me. If Greenfield requests SLA credits, route to Legal/Finance and flag to me. Jonas — keep the ticket updated (SUP-5347).

We’ll follow up with the postmortem and timeline; tagging execs for awareness.
